fields.meaning: Try to…, as much as possible (なるべく早く)
examples: Please reply as soon as possible.
I try to exercise every day if I can.
Please avoid eating sweets as much as possible.

fields.meaning: Get used to…, be used to…
examples: Have you gotten used to life in Japan yet?
I've gradually gotten used to my new job.
I'm not used to getting up early in the morning.

fields.meaning: …, I wonder? (polite question, softens the question)
fields.connection: V plain form + のでしょうか んでしょうか / N + な / Na / Aい
examples: Does this train stop at Tokyo Station?
I wonder why he didn't come.
Would it be all right to use this seat?

fields.meaning: Furthermore, in addition, even more…
examples: Because of the typhoon, the rain got even heavier.
This shop is cheap. Furthermore, the service is good too.
I hear the fees will go up even more next year.

fields.meaning: At most…, at the very most…
examples: Even on foot, it's 10 minutes at most from here to the station.
Probably 20 people at most will come to the party.
The most I can spend on lunch is 1,000 yen.

fields.meaning: A moment, for a while…
examples: Please wait a moment.
I had taken a break from studying Japanese for a while.
I haven't seen him for a while.

fields.meaning: Already… (the action was completed beforehand)
examples: The meeting has already started.
When I arrived at the station, the train had already left.
I already know about that news.

fields.name: Quantity＋は
fields.meaning: At least… (quantity+は)
examples: It takes at least 30 minutes to get to the station.
This bag probably costs at least 20,000 yen.
At least 100 people had gathered at the venue.

fields.name: ～たものだ（reminiscing）
fields.meaning: Used to often…, would often… (reminiscing)
examples: When I was a child, I often used to swim in this river.
In my student days, I used to talk with my friends until morning.
My father says he often used to climb mountains when he was young.

fields.meaning: Certainly…, indeed…
examples: This dish is certainly delicious, but it's too expensive.
What he says is certainly correct.
I'm sure I locked it, but it's open.

fields.meaning: Only need… and that's enough, can be settled with…
examples: The repair only cost 5,000 yen.
If it's something that can be handled by phone, you don't have to go.
Luckily, the injury was only minor.

fields.meaning: So as not to…, in case… (guarding against a bad situation)
examples: I'll make a note in case I forget.
Take a jacket with you so you don't catch a cold.
Let's leave early in case we're late.

fields.meaning: This is no time to… (～ている場合じゃない)
examples: Now is no time to be laughing.
This is no time to be playing games. You have an exam tomorrow!
This is no time to be taking it easy. Let's hurry.

fields.meaning: Suffix 的: turns a noun into a Na-adjective/adverb (経済的)
examples: That way of thinking is not realistic.
Please explain more concretely.
He gave up studying abroad for financial reasons.

fields.meaning: Even if you…, it's no use; …won't do any good
examples: It's no use regretting it now.
Complaining won't get us anywhere, so let's start over.
Worrying won't help. All we can do is wait for the results.

fields.meaning: Apparently…, it seems… (とみえる/とみえて)
fields.connection: V plain form + と見える とみえる とみえて / N + だ / Na + だ / Aい
examples: He seemed to be tired, as he fell asleep right away.
This shop must be popular, because it's always crowded.
It must have rained, because the road is wet.

fields.meaning: In the middle of…, on the way… (途中で/途中に)
examples: On my way to school, I ran into my teacher.
A phone call came in the middle of the meeting.
On the way home, I stopped by the supermarket.

fields.meaning: Cannot possibly…, can hardly… (とても～ない)
examples: There's no way I can solve such a difficult problem.
I can hardly believe that he's the culprit.
I'm so busy that I can't possibly make time to go on a trip.

fields.meaning: Setting… aside, apart from…
fields.connection: N + は別として はべつとして / V plain form + かどうか / Na + かどうか / Aい + かどうか
examples: Joking aside, what are you really planning to do?
Whether or not we go aside, let's at least hear what they have to say.
Design aside, its functions are very good.

fields.meaning: Famous for… (～で有名)
examples: Kyoto is famous for its old temples.
This town is famous for its hot springs.
That teacher is famous for giving a lot of homework.

fields.meaning: On purpose, deliberately…
examples: I think he lost on purpose.
I didn't do it on purpose. I'm sorry.
My younger brother deliberately pretended not to hear.

fields.meaning: Rather than…, compared with… (よりも)
fields.connection: V plain form + よりも / N
examples: This winter is colder than last year.
The process is more important than the result.
The exam was easier than I had expected.

fields.meaning: Looks like…, seems… (ように見える)
fields.connection: V plain form + ように見える / N + の / Na / Aい
examples: He looks like he's angry.
This plan looks simple, but it's actually difficult.
From a distance, it looks like an island.

fields.meaning: No matter what…, at all costs…
examples: I want to get into this university no matter what.
No matter how hard I try, I can't remember his name.
I have something I absolutely have to go to.

fields.meaning: Suddenly…, all of a sudden, without thinking…
examples: When I happened to look out the window, it was snowing.
I suddenly remembered my childhood.
I suddenly woke up in the middle of the night.

fields.meaning: At the same time, at once…
examples: If you eat a lot at once, you'll upset your stomach.
It's impossible to carry all the luggage at once.
Please ask your questions one at a time.

fields.meaning: What on earth…, …in the world (emphasizes a question)
examples: Who on earth did this?
What on earth is this?
Where on earth did he go?

fields.meaning: Surely not…, no way…
fields.connection: まさか + [negative sentence/clause] (～ないだろう)
examples: I never imagined he would lie.
Who would have thought I'd run into my teacher in a place like this!
Surely it won't rain.

fields.meaning: Rather…, more accurately…
examples: Walking is actually faster than taking a taxi.
He's more like a friend than a teacher.
Getting help actually makes it take longer.

fields.meaning: Accidentally…, couldn't help… (unintentionally)
fields.connection: つい + V (usually Vてしまう)
examples: Even though I'm on a diet, I couldn't help eating some cake.
It was so interesting that I ended up reading until midnight.
I carelessly let the secret slip.

fields.meaning: Finally…, in the end… (ついに)
examples: The long construction work ended, and the new station was finally completed.
After 10 years, he finally made his dream come true.
I called many times, but in the end he never answered.

fields.meaning: Go to the trouble of…, take the trouble to… (わざわざ)
examples: Thanks for going to the trouble of coming to pick me up at the station.
You don't have to go all the way to buy it. You can order it online.
Thank you very much for coming all this way.

fields.meaning: Quite, fairly…
examples: It's quite cold today, isn't it?
His Japanese has gotten quite good.
It will take quite a lot of time to complete.

fields.meaning: Whether… differs depending on…
fields.connection: [question] + かは + N + によって違う
examples: What people find delicious differs from person to person.
What students do after graduation differs from student to student.
How much it costs depends on the season.

fields.meaning: Each, each one…
examples: Everyone has their own way of thinking.
Each participant presented their own opinion.
Culture differs from country to country.

fields.meaning: If possible… (modest request)
examples: If possible, I'd like to receive a reply by tomorrow.
If possible, I'd like a window seat, please.
If possible, I'd like you to change the meeting time.

fields.meaning: If… is fine (humble: 私でよければ)
examples: If I'm good enough, I'll help you.
If a used one is fine, you can buy it cheaply.
If tomorrow is fine, I have time.

fields.meaning: In terms of…, speaking of…
examples: Vietnamese "pho" is something like ramen in Japan.
In terms of price, this one is a better deal.
In terms of size, this room is about as big as a classroom.

fields.meaning: It can be said that…
fields.connection: V/A plain form + と言える / N/Naだ + と言える
examples: This result can probably be called a success.
He can be said to be one of the most famous athletes in the world.
An investigation is needed until it can be said to be safe.

fields.name: 代（fee・cost）
fields.meaning: Suffix 代: fee, cost (電気代, バス代)
examples: The electricity bill was high this month.
The company pays for the bus fare.
Meals cost about 3,000 yen per person.
